title: Integers & percent
blurb: Positive and negative numbers, and anything out of 100.

signs.name: Multiplying signs
signs.phrase: Friends are positive. Strangers are negative.
signs.also: Same signs give +. Different signs give −.
steps: Same signs (friends): the answer is positive.
Different signs (strangers): the answer is negative.
signs.exception: This is only for × and ÷. Adding is different: −3 + −4 is −7, not +7. Anything times 0 is 0, with no sign.

intadd.name: Adding integers
intadd.phrase: Same signs: add and keep. Different signs: subtract and keep the bigger one’s sign.
steps: Same: add the sizes, keep the sign.
Different: subtract the smaller size from the bigger, and keep the sign of the bigger size.
intadd.exception: Do not use the friends-and-strangers rule here. −3 + −4 is −7, because adding two debts makes a bigger debt.

percent.name: Percent of a number
percent.phrase: Per cent means out of 100. Hop the decimal two places, then multiply.
steps: Write the percent out of 100: 25% is 0.25.
For a change, always compare with the starting amount.
percent.exception: 10% of 10% is 1%, not 20%. More than 100% is fine: 150% of 40 is 60.

intsub.name: Subtracting integers
intsub.also: Subtracting a number is the same as adding its opposite.
steps: Change the sign of the second number.
intsub.exception: Change both things: the sign in the middle and the second number. Never change the first number. Don’t mix it up with “Keep, Change, Flip” for dividing fractions.

intdiv.name: Dividing integers
intdiv.phrase: Divide the sizes. Same signs, positive. Different signs, negative.
intdiv.also: It is the same sign rule as for ×.
steps: Same signs: the answer is positive.
Different signs: the answer is negative.
intdiv.exception: You can never divide by 0. 0 divided by any other number is 0, with no sign. Two negatives make a positive only for × and ÷, not for + or −.

equations.name: Solving equations
equations.phrase: Do the opposite to both sides.
equations.also: Undo in reverse order: + and − first, then × and ÷.
steps: See what is being done to x.
Undo the + or − first: do the opposite to both sides.
Then undo the × or ÷ the same way.
Check: put your answer back in.
equations.exception: Whatever you do to one side, do to the other, or the two sides stop being equal. Undo the + or − before the ×: in 3x + 4 = 19, don’t divide 19 by 3 first.

circle.name: Circumference and area of a circle
circle.phrase: Cherry pie’s delicious: C = πd. Apple pies are too: A = πr².
circle.also: The diameter goes all the way across. The radius goes halfway: d = 2 × r.
steps: Find the radius r or the diameter d. d = 2 × r.
Around the edge (circumference): C = π × d.
circle.exception: Area uses the radius, not the diameter. If you are given d, halve it first. r² means r × r, not r × 2.

interest.name: Simple interest
interest.phrase: I = PRT: Interest = Principal × Rate × Time.
interest.also: Principal is the money you start with. Rate is the percent per year. Time is in years.
steps: Write the rate as a decimal: 5% = 0.05.
Write the time in years: 6 months = 0.5.
For the total, add the interest to the principal.
interest.exception: Use the rate as a decimal, not the whole number: 5% is 0.05, not 5. Simple interest is the same every year. It does not grow on itself (that is compound interest).

pchange.name: Percent increase and decrease
pchange.phrase: New minus old, over old, times 100.
steps: Multiply by 100 to get a percent. Positive is an increase, negative is a decrease.
pchange.exception: Always divide by the old number, not the new one. Up 50% then down 50% does not bring you back: 100 → 150 → 75.

discount.name: Discount and sales tax
discount.phrase: Sale? Take it off. Tax? Put it on.
discount.also: 20% off means you pay 80%. 5% tax means you pay 105%.
steps: Find the percent of the price.
Discount: subtract it from the price.
Tax: add it to the price.
Both: take the discount off first, then find the tax on the new price.
discount.exception: Tax goes on the sale price, not the old price. 20% off and then 5% tax is not the same as 15% off.

prob.name: Probability
prob.phrase: What you want, over all you’ve got.
prob.exception: The total includes the ones you want. With 3 red and 5 blue, P(red) is 3/8, not 3/5. A probability is always from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).

proportion.name: Proportions
proportion.also: Multiply across each diagonal. The two wings are equal. Then divide by the number next to x.
steps: Set up two equal fractions, with the same order on both sides.
Multiply across the diagonals: the butterfly wings.
Set the wings equal and divide to find x.
proportion.exception: Only cross multiply when two fractions are equal. Never do it to add fractions. Keep the order the same: miles over hours = miles over hours.

dirt-distance.name: Distance = rate × time
dirt-distance.also: Distance, rate, time share one triangle of formulas.
dirt-distance.exception: Units must match. Average speed ≠ instantaneous speed.

speed-triangle.name: D–S–T cover-up
speed-triangle.phrase: Distance = speed × time; cover up the unknown in the D–S–T relation.
steps: Identify which of D, S, T you need.
Cover that letter: the other two show multiply or divide.
Use D = ST, S = D ÷ T, or T = D ÷ S.
speed-triangle.exception: Use consistent units. Average speed is total distance ÷ total time — not the average of speeds.

scalene-odd-one.name: Scalene triangles
scalene-odd-one.phrase: Scalene is the odd one out: no equal sides.
scalene-odd-one.also: Equilateral: all equal. Isosceles: at least two equal.
steps: Two equal → isosceles; three equal → equilateral.
scalene-odd-one.exception: Side names ≠ angle names (acute/right/obtuse). A scalene triangle can still be acute, right, or obtuse.

kcc.name: Keep Change Change
kcc.phrase: Keep Change Change: keep the first, change − to +, change the next sign.
kcc.also: Subtracting a negative is adding: a − (−b) = a + b.
steps: Change the sign of the second number.
kcc.exception: KCC is for subtraction of integers. Don’t KCC a multiplication.

arithspell.name: Spelling arithmetic
arithspell.phrase: A Rat In The House May Eat The Ice Cream.
steps: Write A R I T H M E T I C.
arithspell.exception: It’s a spelling hook — not a calculation method.

commute7.name: Integer properties
commute7.phrase: Flip and regroup still work with negatives for + and ×.
steps: Commutative: order can flip for + and ×.
commute7.exception: Subtraction isn’t commutative even with KCC — rewrite as adding the opposite first.

distrib7.name: Distribute with signs
distrib7.phrase: Give the outside factor — including its sign — to each term inside.
steps: Write a(b + c) as ab + ac.
If outside is negative, every term flips sign.

wordkeys7.name: Integer word clues
wordkeys7.phrase: Altogether still adds; left still subtracts — now signs can be negative.
steps: Attach signs from the story (debt, below, loss).
wordkeys7.exception: “More than” on a number line can mean move positive even if you started negative.

estimate7.name: Estimate percents
estimate7.phrase: Round the amount, use a friendly percent, then adjust.
steps: Scale up to the percent you need.
estimate7.exception: Estimates for tips/tax are fine; bank interest needs exact.

absval.name: Absolute value
absval.phrase: Absolute value is distance from zero — always positive (or zero).
steps: Find how far the number is from 0.
absval.exception: |−3| = 3, but that doesn’t make −3 positive in every equation — context matters.

unitrate7.name: Unit rate
unitrate7.phrase: Find the rate for one, and then you’re done.
steps: Multiply the unit rate for more.
unitrate7.exception: Keep units matched: miles per hour, not miles per minute mixed in.

cross7.name: Cross multiply solve
cross7.phrase: Butterfly: cross multiply, then divide to free x.
steps: Divide by the coefficient of x.
cross7.exception: Only when two ratios are equal — not for adding fractions.

scale7.name: Scale factor
scale7.phrase: New = old × scale. Scale >1 grows; between 0 and 1 shrinks.
scale7.exception: A scale of 2 doubles lengths, but area becomes ×4.

opposites7.name: Additive inverses
opposites7.phrase: A number plus its opposite makes zero.
opposites7.exception: Opposite of 0 is 0. Opposite is not the same as reciprocal.

taxest7.name: Mental tax & tip
taxest7.phrase: 10% hop the decimal; 20% is double that; 15% is 10% + half of 10%.
steps: Find 10% by moving the decimal one left.
Add to the bill for tip/tax.
taxest7.exception: Exact tax rates may be 6.25% — estimate first, then calculate exactly if needed.

orderint7.name: Order with negatives
orderint7.phrase: On the number line, left is smaller — even if the digits look bigger.

convert7.name: Fraction–decimal–percent
convert7.phrase: Percent is hundredths; hop the decimal two places.
convert7.exception: 1/3 is 0.333… repeating — percent ≈ 33.3%, not a tidy terminating decimal.

mental7.name: Mental integer chains
mental7.phrase: Do easy jumps on the number line: +10, −10, then the leftovers.
steps: Chunk the second number into friendly jumps.
mental7.exception: Don’t reverse a jump direction when signs get messy — rewrite with KCC first if subtracting.
